centralSubsidies.name: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana central financial assistance (CFA)
centralSubsidies.description: CFA for residential rooftop solar: 60% of the benchmark cost for the first 2 kWp and 40% for the 3rd kWp; nothing beyond 3 kWp. Made-in-India modules with Indian cells are mandatory. Applied for through the national portal; the CFA is not tied to inverter size.

installedCost.note: MNRE benchmark cost used to compute the CFA (first 2 kW at Rs 50,000/kW, additional kW at Rs 45,000/kW, from 13 Feb 2024). It is a scheme reference, not a market price: 2026 market quotes for a 3 kW system are often Rs 1.65-2.1 lakh before subsidy. Use your vendor's quote when you have one.

cite.quote: The benchmark cost for 1 kW system is fixed at Rs 50,000/kW for the first 2 kW of RTS capacity and Rs 45,000 for the additional kW

assumptions.label: Typical 2026 market price, residential rooftop (before subsidy)
assumptions.note: Midpoint of the Rs 1.65-2.1 lakh range quoted for 3 kW systems. Indicative market prices, not verified quotes.

assumptions.label: Performance ratio
assumptions.note: PM Surya Ghar vendors must deliver PR 75% at commissioning and maintain it through the 5-year warranty. Used as the simulator default.

cite.quote: The Performance Ratio (PR) of Plant must be 75% at the time of commissioning

assumptions.label: Module degradation implied by the warranty floor
assumptions.note: PM Surya Ghar modules must keep >90% of rated output for 10 years and >80% for the next 15. 80% after 25 years is about 0.8%/yr. Used as the simulator default.

assumptions.label: Measured degradation of rooftop crystalline modules in India
assumptions.note: NISE / NCPRE IIT Bombay field survey (2018) measured 1.99%/yr for roof-mounted c-Si modules vs 1.33%/yr ground-mounted. Use for a pessimistic case.

cite.quote: the roof-(rack)-mounted modules show a degradation rate of 1.99 %/year

assumptions.label: Useful life of a rooftop plant

cite.quote: the useful life of the plant shall be 25 years

consumerRights.summary: Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, rule 5(7): the distribution licensee must test the meter within thirty days of receiving a complaint.

cite.quote: The testing of meters shall be done by the distribution licensee within thirty days of receipt of the complaint

consumerRights.summary: Rule 5(7) proviso (2024 amendment): if you complain that readings are not commensurate with your consumption, the licensee must install an additional meter within five days to verify consumption for at least three months.

cite.quote: Distribution Licensee shall install an additional meter within five days from the date of receipt of the complaint, to verify the consumption, for a minimum period of three months.

consumerRights.summary: Rule 5(11): if you dispute the licensee's test result, the meter is tested at a third-party laboratory you choose from the regulator's approved list; that result is final and binding on both sides.

cite.quote: the said results are final and binding on both the consumer and the distribution licensee

consumerRights.summary: Rule 9(3): a prepaid meter cutting off when credit runs out is not a disconnection, and supply is to be resumed whenever the meter is recharged. The national rules set no number of hours; check your state Supply Code and standards of performance.

cite.quote: This shall however not be treated as a disconnection and the supply will be resumed whenever

consumerRights.summary: Rule 8A (2023 amendment): time-of-day tariffs apply immediately after a smart meter is installed. Solar-hours rates must be at least 20% below normal, and peak rates for domestic consumers at least 1.10 times normal, on the energy charge only.

cite.quote: shall be atleast twenty percent less than the normal tariff for that category of consumers

consumerRights.summary: CEA (Installation and Operation of Meters) Regulations, reg. 15(2) and 18(2): consumers may report readings not commensurate with consumption; meters must be tested on site through an accredited laboratory at least once in five years, and out of cycle when consumption changes drastically.

cite.quote: The testing of Consumer Meters shall be done at site through accredited test laboratory at least once in five years

consumerRights.summary: Electricity Act, 2003, Section 42(5)-(6): every licensee must have a Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum; if it does not resolve your complaint you can appeal to the State Electricity Ombudsman.
